answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. So the design does not rely on catching every cheat — it makes cheating unprofitable, which is a far more stable defense than any whitelist ever could be.. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. Consider a crystal as the anchor of the cost.
